name: Logistics
description: Shipping, delivery, third-party logistics (3PL), and fleet/dispatch operations: rating and booking shipments across carriers, planning and dispatching routes, tracking parcels and vehicles in real time, and capturing proof of delivery.

sources.title: Karrio
sources.notes: reference-only (LGPL). Multi-carrier shipping API/platform. Cloned modules/manager (Address, Parcel, Commodity, Pickup, Tracking, Shipment, DocumentUploadRecord, Manifest models + PickupStatus/ShipmentStatus/TrackerStatus enums in modules/core), and modules/orders (Order model, OrderStatus). The ee/ directory (commercial add-ons, under separate LICENSE_EE) and the rating/providers/connectors modules were not cloned.

sources.title: Fleetbase
sources.notes: reference-only (AGPL). Fleet operations / last-mile dispatch platform. Full DB schema inspected via the repo's own generated database.mmd (Mermaid ERD): orders, payloads, waypoints, routes, drivers, vehicles, fleets, manifests, tracking_statuses, issues, maintenance_schedules/maintenances, service_rates/quotes, places, zones. Application code beyond the schema was not deeply inspected in this pass.

sources.title: GS1 General Specifications (GTIN, SSCC, GS1-128 Application Identifiers)
sources.license: GS1 IP Policy disclaimer (no OSI license; preserve GS1 copyright/disclaimer verbatim)
sources.notes: Defines the GTIN (product identifier), SSCC (18-digit logistic-unit identifier, printed as a GS1-128 barcode with Application Identifier (00)), and the surrounding AI framework. The GS1 Logistic Label Guideline (a GS1 implementation guideline built on these same GS1-128/SSCC primitives) was checked via its gs1.org landing page for existence but its own version/date could not be fetched directly (403); only General Specifications 26.0 is cited with a verified version.

sources.title: UPU S10 - Identification of postal items (13-character identifier)
sources.license: UPU standard, publicly published; no OSI license
sources.notes: 13-character international postal item identifier (2-letter service indicator + 8-digit serial + check digit + 2-letter ISO country code of the issuing postal operator). Relevant to international parcel/label tracking numbers issued by postal operators rather than integrator carriers.

sources.title: UN/EDIFACT IFTMIN (Transport Instruction) and IFCSUM (Forwarding and Consolidation Summary) messages
sources.license: UN/EDIFACT (UNECE/UNTDID), publicly published; no OSI license
sources.version: UNTDID message directory (multiple co-existing releases, e.g. D.03B through D.12A+; no single current release number independently pinned in this pass)
sources.notes: IFTMIN is the shipper/forwarder-to-carrier transport instruction message for a single consignment (final consignment details, dispatch instruction); IFCSUM is the forwarding/consolidation summary message describing consolidated cargo on a voyage/consignment run. Read via UNECE's own service.unece.org message-directory pages and corroborating summaries, not fetched as a full page in this pass; message existence, purpose and field-level intent are confirmed, exact current release edition is not.

sources.title: UN/CEFACT Multi-Modal Transport Reference Data Model (MMT RDM)
sources.license: UN/CEFACT (UNECE), publicly published; no OSI license
sources.version: Multi-Modal Transport Reference Data Model BRS (Business Requirements Specification), part of the UN/CEFACT global Buy-Ship-Pay / Supply Chain Reference Data Model
sources.notes: Technical specifications and data structures (subsets, XSDs) for documents accompanying goods moved across sea/inland-water/air/road/rail legs. Corroborates the general shape of multi-leg/multi-stop consignment and transport-plan data, not a route-optimization algorithm. Read via search-indexed UNECE page summaries in this pass, not the full BRS document text.

sources.title: ASC X12 transportation transaction sets 204/990/214/210
sources.license: ASC X12 standard; official transaction-set text is a paid X12.org publication and was not accessed directly
sources.version: Set numbers verified: 204 (Motor Carrier Load Tender), 990 (Response to Load Tender), 214 (Transportation Carrier Shipment Status), 210 (Motor Carrier Freight Details and Invoice); X12 version/release (e.g. 004010/005010) not independently confirmed
sources.notes: Corroborated across multiple independent EDI service-provider documentation pages (SPS Commerce, EDI2XML, 1EDISource, EDI Elevate) describing the same four set numbers and the same tender->accept->status->invoice flow. Marked source_type 'secondary' rather than 'authoritative' because the official ASC X12 standard text itself (X12.org) was not accessed.

sources.title: IATA e-AWB (Resolution 672) and Cargo-XML Toolkit
sources.license: IATA standard; publicly described on iata.org, full toolkit is a member publication
sources.version: e-AWB: IATA Resolution 672 (Multilateral e-AWB Agreement, paper AWB no longer required); Cargo-XML: current IATA Cargo-XML Toolkit (successor to the retired Cargo-IMP message set since 2014)
sources.notes: Air-freight-specific electronic air waybill and the XML messaging standard used between airlines, forwarders, ground handlers, customs and security agencies.

sources.title: Incoterms 2020
sources.license: ICC copyrighted rules; publicly summarized, full text is a paid ICC publication
sources.version: Incoterms 2020 (effective 1 January 2020), 11 rules, each with A1-A10/B1-B10 seller/buyer obligations
sources.notes: Standardizes where risk, cost, and delivery/customs responsibility transfer between buyer and seller for a given shipment; used here for the responsibility-transfer dimension of customs and shipment features, never as evidence that a product is legally compliant.

sources.title: WCO Data Model
sources.license: World Customs Organization standard; publicly described, full data model publication has WCO usage terms
sources.version: 4.3.0 (approved by WCO Council June 2026, presented July 2026)
sources.notes: Harmonized customs data elements and packages (goods declaration, AEO mutual recognition, passenger/crew advance information, etc.) used by customs administrations worldwide; cited for the customs-declaration data-modeling dimension of logistics.customs_documents only, not as proof of customs compliance.

sources.title: ADR - European Agreement concerning the International Carriage of Dangerous Goods by Road
sources.license: UNECE treaty text, publicly published; no OSI license
sources.notes: Road dangerous-goods classification, packaging, marking, labelling, documentation and vehicle/driver requirements across 53 contracting parties.

sources.title: IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations (DGR)
sources.license: IATA standard; publicly described, full manual is a paid IATA publication
sources.notes: Global reference for classifying, packaging, marking, labelling and documenting dangerous goods shipped by air; the only DG standard recognized by airlines.

sources.title: IMDG Code - International Maritime Dangerous Goods Code
sources.license: IMO instrument, publicly described; full code is a paid IMO publication
sources.version: 2024 Edition, Amendment 42-24 (voluntary from 1 January 2025, mandatory from 1 January 2026)
sources.notes: Sea dangerous-goods classification, packing, marking and documentation requirements, published in two volumes plus a supplement.

sources.title: Traccar
sources.version: HEAD (default branch) at retrieval time, verified via `gh api repos/traccar/traccar`
sources.notes: Read only via `gh api` (not cloned to disk), per the research brief's no-new-downloads rule. Open-source GPS/telematics platform (200+ device protocols). Inspected src/main/java/org/traccar/model/{Device,Driver,Position,Geofence,Maintenance}.java: Device/Position carry live telemetry (odometer, engine hours, fuel level/consumption, battery, GPS position); Geofence carries a named boundary with schedule; Maintenance carries name/type/start/period (interval-based service scheduling); Driver is a thin name+uniqueId record. Independent second implementation for vehicle telemetry, geofencing, fuel tracking, and (thinly) driver and fleet-maintenance concepts, alongside fleetbase.

features.name: Customers and shippers
features.description: Accounts for the businesses or individuals who book shipments and orders, with saved addresses and billing details.

provenance.notes: Both platforms scope shipments/orders under an owning account (karrio OwnedEntity, fleetbase company_uuid).

features.name: Orders
features.description: A customer's request to move goods, capturing line items and delivery details before it is turned into one or more shipments or dispatched jobs.

provenance.notes: karrio's orders module (Order, OrderStatus) and fleetbase_orders are independent implementations. UN/EDIFACT IFTMIN is the standard message that turns an order/instruction into a transport contract for a consignment, corroborating the order-to-shipment concept from an authoritative standards source.

features.name: Shipments
features.description: A booked movement of one or more parcels with a carrier, tracking number, label, and status from creation through delivery.

provenance.notes: karrio's Shipment model is the direct implementation. GS1 EPCIS 2.0 (std:gs1-epcis, verified on disk) models exactly this concept as a trackable object moving through ObjectEvent/AggregationEvent scans (what/when/where/why), and GS1 General Specifications' SSCC is the identifier standard for the logistic unit a shipment represents. Authoritative source present.

features.name: Parcels and packages
features.description: The physical package(s) within a shipment: dimensions, weight, and the commodities/products packed inside.

provenance.notes: karrio's Parcel/Commodity models are the direct implementation. GS1 General Specifications defines the GTIN (product inside) and SSCC (the physical logistic unit/parcel itself, printed as GS1-128); EPCIS's epcList/quantityList 'what' dimension is the standard's model of the same physical-object concept. Authoritative source present.

features.name: Rates and quotes
features.description: Requesting and comparing shipping rates across carriers and service levels before a shipment is booked.

provenance.notes: karrio's Shipment.rates/selected_rate fields and fleetbase's fleetbase_purchase_rates/fleetbase_service_quotes tables (already cross-referenced for the rate_quote entity) are independent implementations of the same concept; the rating/providers module itself was not cloned from karrio.

features.name: Carriers and carrier connections
features.description: The shipping carriers (and their service levels/accounts) a business ships with; a snapshot is stored on each shipment.

provenance.notes: karrio's Shipment.carrier snapshot (JSON, keyed by carrier_code, indexed) is the only directly-inspected evidence; single source.

features.name: Shipping labels
features.description: Generating and storing the carrier shipping label (and commercial invoice) document for a purchased shipment.

provenance.notes: karrio's Shipment.label/label_type/invoice fields are the direct implementation. The GS1 Logistic Label / GS1-128 symbology is the authoritative standard for what a carrier-agnostic logistics label actually encodes (SSCC via Application Identifier (00)); UPU S10 is the parallel standard for the identifier printed on international postal labels. Authoritative source present.

features.name: Manifests
features.description: Grouping shipments or stops into a single hand-off: a carrier close-out manifest for end-of-day pickup, or a driver's route manifest for the day's stops.

provenance.notes: karrio's carrier close-out Manifest model and fleetbase's driver route fleetbase_manifests table are independent implementations of a shipment/stop grouping. GS1's SSCC is the authoritative standard identifier for exactly this kind of grouped 'logistic unit' handed off as a batch. Authoritative source present.

features.name: Pickup scheduling
features.description: Scheduling a carrier or driver pickup for one or more shipments at a given time window.

provenance.notes: karrio's Pickup model and PickupStatus enum (scheduled/picked_up/cancelled/closed) is the direct implementation. UN/EDIFACT IFTMIN is the standard shipper-to-carrier instruction message that, among other things, carries pickup/collection scheduling details for a consignment, corroborating the general concept from a second, independent (standards) source.

features.name: Tracking events
features.description: The append-only timeline of scan/status events for a shipment or parcel, from pickup through delivery, shown to customers and staff.

provenance.notes: karrio's TrackerStatus enum and fleetbase's fleetbase_tracking_statuses table are independent implementations. GS1 EPCIS 2.0 (verified on disk) is the authoritative supply-chain event-visibility standard for exactly this concept (what/when/where/why per event). Authoritative source present.

features.name: Proof of delivery
features.description: Capturing a photo and/or signature at the moment of delivery and attaching it to the shipment/order record.

provenance.notes: karrio's TrackingStatus.delivery_image_url/signature_image_url fields and fleetbase's payloads.pod_method/pod_required fields both model this independently.

features.name: Dispatch
features.description: Assigning a driver and vehicle to an order or route and releasing it for execution.

provenance.notes: fleetbase_orders' dispatched/dispatched_at/adhoc/driver_assigned_uuid/vehicle_assigned_uuid columns are the direct implementation. UN/EDIFACT IFTMIN is the standard message by which a shipper instructs a carrier/forwarder to move a consignment, i.e. the EDI-level equivalent of dispatching a job.

features.name: Routes and route optimization
features.description: Sequencing an order's or manifest's stops (waypoints) into an efficient route, with distance/time totals.

provenance.notes: fleetbase_routes/fleetbase_waypoints tables are the direct implementation. UN/CEFACT's Multi-Modal Transport Reference Data Model standardizes multi-leg/multi-stop consignment and transport-plan data structures, corroborating the general shape of a sequenced route/waypoint plan; it does not standardize a route-optimization algorithm, so this is a data-structure-level corroboration only.

features.name: Drivers
features.description: Driver profiles, licensing, current location, availability, and skills used for dispatch and compliance.

provenance.notes: fleetbase_drivers table is the direct implementation. traccar's Driver model (name, uniqueId, associated with device/position events) is a second, independent but thin implementation read via `gh api` without cloning; kept at medium rather than high because traccar's driver model itself is minimal.

features.name: Vehicles
features.description: The fleet's vehicles: specifications, capacity, and current telemetry (location, speed, heading).

provenance.notes: fleetbase_vehicles table (make/model/year, capacities, fuel_type, location/speed/heading) and traccar's Device+Position models (odometer, engine hours, fuel, battery, GPS position) are independent implementations of vehicle/telemetry data, read via `gh api` without cloning.

features.name: Warehouses and locations
features.description: Physical facilities (warehouses, depots, hubs) where inventory is stored or shipments are consolidated.

provenance.notes: Neither cloned implementation models a warehouse as a first-class entity, so this remains standards-only rather than implementation-corroborated. GS1 EPCIS's bizLocation/readPoint fields and CBV business steps (receiving, storing, staging_outbound, stocking) model warehouse-type facilities as event context; GS1 General Specifications defines the GLN (Global Location Number) used to identify such facilities. Kept at medium, not high, because there is still no product-feature implementation observed, only the underlying identifier/location concepts.

features.name: Exceptions and returns
features.description: Flagging delivery problems (damage, delay, failed attempt) for investigation, and processing return shipments back to origin.
ai_opportunities: auto-triage exception type from scan text

provenance.notes: fleetbase_issues table and karrio's needs_attention/delivery_failed/return_shipment fields are independent implementations. GS1 CBV's disposition vocabulary (damaged, destroyed, returned, recalled, stolen, non_conformant, etc.) is the authoritative standard vocabulary for exactly these exception/return states. Authoritative source present.

features.name: Customs documents
features.description: Customs declaration data (commodities, values, HS codes) required for international shipments.
ai_opportunities: HS code suggestion from product description

provenance.notes: karrio's Shipment.customs embedded field is the direct implementation. The WCO Data Model is the authoritative harmonized data model for customs (goods) declarations; Incoterms 2020 standardizes the responsibility-transfer/cost-allocation data a customs declaration and commercial invoice both depend on. Authoritative source present. Citing these standards is not a claim that any implementation is customs-compliant.

features.name: Driver mobile app
features.description: The driver-facing mobile app for viewing assigned stops, navigating, updating status, capturing proof of delivery, and working with limited or no connectivity.

provenance.notes: Inferred from fleetbase's driver-oriented schema (drivers, manifests, waypoints with service_time/time windows); no mobile client code was inspected, single source, reasoned.

features.name: Zones and geofencing
features.description: Named geographic zones (service areas, geofences) used for pricing, routing eligibility, and driver/vehicle geofence entry-exit events.

provenance.notes: fleetbase_zones/fleetbase_service_areas/geofence_states tables and traccar's Geofence model (named boundary with schedule) are independent implementations of the same concept, read via `gh api` without cloning.

features.name: Fleet maintenance
features.description: Scheduling recurring vehicle maintenance (by date, distance, or engine hours) and recording completed service.

provenance.notes: fleetbase_maintenance_schedules (interval_method/type/value, next_due_date, reminder_offsets) and traccar's Maintenance model (name/type/start/period) are independent implementations of interval-based vehicle service scheduling, read via `gh api` without cloning.

features.name: Address validation
features.description: Verifying and normalizing shipping addresses before a label is purchased, to reduce failed deliveries.

provenance.notes: karrio's Address model with a dedicated AddressManager; single source, reasoned that validation is a common capability layered on top of it.

features.name: Contract and negotiated rates
features.description: Custom rate cards or markups negotiated with a carrier, applied instead of or alongside published rates.

provenance.notes: fleetbase_service_rates/service_rate_fees/service_rate_parcel_fees/purchase_rates tables; single source, karrio's own rate-sheet PRDs mention this too but were not inspected (docs only, not code).

features.name: Claims
features.description: Filing and tracking damage or loss claims against a carrier for a shipment.

provenance.notes: Reasoned extension of fleetbase's fleetbase_issues (damage/loss category) toward a carrier claim; no dedicated claims table found in either source.

features.name: Fuel tracking
features.description: Recording fuel purchases and consumption per vehicle, optionally synced from a fuel card provider.

provenance.notes: fleetbase_fuel_provider_connections/sync_runs/transactions tables and traccar's Position telemetry fields (KEY_FUEL, KEY_FUEL_USED, KEY_FUEL_CONSUMPTION, KEY_FUEL_LEVEL) are independent implementations of per-vehicle fuel data, read via `gh api` without cloning.

features.name: Cash on delivery
features.description: Collecting payment from the recipient at the time of delivery instead of billing the shipper upfront.

provenance.notes: fleetbase_payloads.cod_amount/cod_currency/cod_payment_method columns; single source.

features.name: ETA prediction
features.description: Estimating and updating a delivery's arrival window using live route, traffic, and historical performance data.
ai_opportunities: ML ETA model from historical route performance

provenance.notes: Reasoned from route total_distance/total_time and waypoint time_window fields; no ML/ETA code inspected, single source.

features.name: Driver performance scoring
features.description: Scorecards for on-time rate, safety incidents, and customer feedback per driver.

provenance.notes: Reasoned from fleetbase_issues (driver_uuid, category, priority); no dedicated scorecard table found, single source.

features.name: Load planning
features.description: Consolidating multiple parcels or orders into a single vehicle load, respecting capacity and compatibility constraints.

provenance.notes: Reasoned from fleetbase_vehicles.payload_capacity and order/parcel volume fields; no dedicated load-planning table found, single source, low confidence.

features.name: Freight invoicing and audit
features.description: Reconciling carrier invoices against quoted/contracted rates and flagging billing discrepancies.

provenance.notes: karrio's Shipment.applied_fees field is the direct implementation. ASC X12 210 (Motor Carrier Freight Details and Invoice) is the standard EDI transaction set for exactly this document, corroborated across multiple independent EDI service-provider descriptions (official X12.org text not accessed).
